=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- docs/plans/remove-unattended-pipeline-stuck-states-plan.md:314-315 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: The plan states "Apply ai:needs-human" on exhaustion (line 314) and says the item "becomes eligible again" on a trusted human comment, label change, or new head SHA, which only resets the round count (line 315). It does not specify whether the ai:needs-human label itself is cleared on trigger, so a comment-only trigger leaves the label set and the item still in BLOCK_LABELS with judge rounds skipped.
  WHY: During implementation, an implementer following this spec literally would reset the round counter while ai:needs-human remains applied, so the poller continues skipping judge rounds for that item despite the trigger having fired. The documented "becomes eligible again" promise cannot be fulfilled without also clearing the label or exempting triggered items from BLOCK_LABELS checks.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- docs/plans/remove-unattended-pipeline-stuck-states-plan.md:313-315 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: P6 applies `ai:needs-human` to parked items and says "skip new judge rounds for parked items" because the label is in `BLOCK_LABELS`. It then says a parked item "becomes eligible again only on a new trigger: a comment from a trusted human, a label change by a human, or a new head SHA. That trigger resets the item's round count to 0." The plan never says the trigger removes `ai:needs-human`. Two of the three triggers (trusted-human comment, new head SHA) do not by themselves clear the label, so the round count is reset to 0 but the item is still in `BLOCK_LABELS`, so the poller continues to skip it. Only the "label change by a human" trigger happens to imply label removal, and only when that change is removing `ai:needs-human` specifically. Items that exhaust rounds therefore cannot re-enter the judge queue, defeating the explicit plan goal "the pipeline must retry with an LLM … only then hand off to a person".
  WHY: When P6 is later implemented, an item that triggers on a non-label-change event (trusted comment, new head SHA) will keep `ai:needs-human` set, the poller's `BLOCK_LABELS` skip will keep excluding it from judge rounds, and the human hand-off never re-converges. The plan needs to explicitly say the trigger also removes `ai:needs-human` (or specifically says "label change by a human" means removing that label) so all three triggers clear the block.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py (also workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py): line 544 (warning emit) and line 1498 (consumer check) | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: The new commit path is wired through a string-equality match against `invocation.warning == "could not resolve env -C directory"`. The consumer at line 1498 only fires if the warning string emitted at line 544 is byte-identical. If a future refactor rewrites the warning text (a routine copy edit or i18n pass), the `commit` branch silently falls through to the existing flow. That existing flow constructs a `_GuardTarget` for the commit (since `_push_targets` is push-only), the `if target.warning: _warn(target.warning)` at line 1525 fires, `_warn` only appends to `system_messages` (not `ask_reasons`), and no `_request_confirmation` is invoked. The hook then returns `code=0, message=""` with no `permissionDecision: ask` in the JSON. The previous behavior — silently checking the session checkout — returns. The `tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py` test `test_env_unresolved_commit_directory_asks_instead_of_checking_checkout` (line 1425) catches this regression only if someone runs the test after the refactor; a warning-text drift is not statically detectable from `_guarded_git_invocations`.
  WHY: A refactor that changes the literal at line 544 silently re-enables the unsafe "fall back to the session checkout for unresolvable `env -C` commits" path the changelog explicitly removes. The hook is safety-critical (CLAUDE.md §21), and the warning-string is the only link between producer and consumer.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
- docs/plans/remove-unattended-pipeline-stuck-states-plan.md:314-315 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The plan says a parked item "becomes eligible again" when a trusted human comment, label change, or new head SHA fires, and that the trigger "resets the item's round count to 0." But line 314 also states "`ai:needs-human` is itself in `BLOCK_LABELS`: skip new judge rounds for parked items." The plan never specifies that the trigger removes `ai:needs-human`. Without label removal, the poller continues to skip judge rounds for the item regardless of the round-count reset, and the item never actually becomes eligible again.
  WHY: After implementation, a human comment or new head SHA resets the counter while `ai:needs-human` remains on the issue. The poller's `BLOCK_LABELS` check still matches, so no new judge round runs. The item is parked permanently until a human manually removes the label — contradicting the plan's promise that the trigger alone restores eligibility. The implementer has no specification for which of the three triggers removes the label, or whether all three do.
=== END FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===

  PROBLEM: The escalation policy specifies that a parked item becomes eligible again on a new trigger (human comment, label change, or new head SHA) that resets its round count to 0, but it never specifies removing the `ai:needs-human` label (or otherwise clearing the parked state). Line 314 states `ai:needs-human` is itself in `BLOCK_LABELS` and that judge rounds are skipped for parked items. With the label still applied and the parked flag still set, the poller would continue skipping judge rounds for the item even after the trigger, so it cannot resume automatically as promised.
  WHY: After implementation, a listed trigger resets the count while the blocking label and parked flag remain, so the poller keeps skipping judge rounds. The item cannot re-enter the unblock judge loop and stays stuck in `ai:needs-human` indefinitely, contradicting the plan's goal that the item "becomes eligible again."
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:1498 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: The new commit-directory-unresolved branch matches the warning by exact string equality against the literal set at line 544. The warning string is duplicated across two sites (the producer at 544 and the consumer at 1498) with no shared constant. A future edit to the warning text at 544 would silently stop the new branch from firing, causing an unresolved `env -C` commit to fall through to the existing path at 1524-1525 that only `_warn`s and checks the session checkout — exactly the §21 behavior this change is meant to remove.
  WHY: The guard's "ask for confirmation" semantics for unresolved `env -C` commits depend on two string literals staying byte-identical. There is no contract test pinning the equality (the diff adds no test for the new branch). A refactor of the warning string silently reverts the safety property.
